unit.title: The Indus Valley and Ancient China

contentBlocks.text: You now know all four great river-valley civilizations. Today: compare them all side by side!

Four civilizations, four rivers: Mesopotamia (the Tigris and Euphrates), Egypt (the Nile), the Indus Valley (the Indus River), and China (the Yellow River). Every one of them grew because a river provided fertile soil, water, and a way to travel and trade. Pick two of the four civilizations and explain one way they were similar, and one way they were different.
You just compared civilizations across two different weeks of learning! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Name all four river-valley civilizations and their rivers
Compare two of the four civilizations, naming one similarity and one difference
materialsNeeded: This week's and last week's worksheets
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review all four civilizations and their rivers together.
2. Model a comparison between two civilizations (e.g., Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley).
3. Have the child pick their own two civilizations and compare them.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a simple 4-row chart (Civilization, River, One Fact) already filled in as a reference for the comparison
Ready for more: ask the child to rank all four civilizations by which achievement they find most impressive, and explain why
This is the two-week synthesis moment — connecting last week's Mesopotamia/Egypt content to this week's Indus Valley/China content into one coherent comparison
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended comparison activity — check that the child picks two real civilizations and states a genuine, accurate similarity and a genuine, accurate difference between them.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's History and Geography dimensions, synthesizing two full weeks of river-valley-civilizations content into one connected comparison before tomorrow's review.
